title: When Kids Got Cocaine for Toothache

sections.name: When Kids Got Cocaine for Toothache
lines: In the 1880s, if your child had a toothache, you could buy cocaine drops at the pharmacy.
They were sold as an instant cure, and the adverts showed happy children playing.
Cocaine really does numb pain. In 1884, it became the first local anaesthetic used in eye surgery.
Soon it was in wines, tonics and even soft drinks.
But it's also highly addictive, and people started getting hooked.
Today, dentists use safer cousins of cocaine, like lidocaine, that numb without the high.
